title: [YouPass Collect] - Positions of Women in Government and Management in five countries: 2000
prompt: The table below shows the information about the posts held by women in parliament and in management in 5 countries in 2000. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table compares the percentages of women holding seats in parliament and managerial positions across five countries in the year 2000.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, female representation in management exceeded that in parliament in all five nations. Additionally, while Norway had the highest proportion of women in parliament, Italy recorded the largest share of female managers.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the countries with stronger parliamentary representation, Norway led the way with 36% of seats held by women, which was 8 percentage points higher than Canada's figure of 28%. In terms of management roles, more than half of all managers in Norway were female, standing at 52%, whereas the corresponding figure for Canada was notably lower at 37%, making it the second lowest among the five surveyed nations.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining three nations, women occupied less than a fifth of parliamentary seats, with Tobago and Trinidad recording 19%, followed by Italy and Uruguay at just 10% and 8%, respectively. However, there was considerable variation in managerial positions among these countries. Specifically, Italy reported the highest figure across all surveyed nations at 54%, despite having one of the lowest parliamentary representations. Meanwhile, Tobago and Trinidad registered 40%, while Uruguay stood at 37%, which was identical to Canada despite having vastly different parliamentary figures.
